To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human epithelial carcinoma (HCA) antigen is a carbohydrate sequence that is distinct from the ABO, Lewis(a/b) and Lewis(x/y) blood group determinants, that it is strongly represented in monosulfated tri- and tetraglycosyl ceramides, and that it is a target for the monoclonal antibody, AE3.

the antigen recognized on epithelial cancers by the monoclonal antibody, AE3, is a carbohydrate sequence, Galβ1,3GalNAc3-O-sulfatβ1,4Galβ1,4GlcC, that is present on both mucin-type glycoproteins and sulfoglycolips.
the antigen recognized with monoclonal antibody (MAb) AE3 is the sulfoglycoliphid SM1a, and that the antigen is expressed not only on HCA glycoproteins but also on a sulfogalactosylceramide, SM1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the antigenic determinant of a monoclonal antibody, AE3, which has been regarded as the most carcinoma-specific antibody in the HCA family.
elucidating the nature of the antigens of the human epithelial carcinoma (HECA) family, which is a group of mucin glycoproteins over-expressed on the surface of epithelial cancers.
elucidating the structure of the antigen recognized by monocloal antibodies raised against the human epithelial carcinoma (HCA) antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AE3 is a highly specific antibody that detects a glycan sequence that is expressed on the sulfoglycolipoprotein SM1a and on the mucins MUC1, MUC2, MUC4 and MUC6.
the HCA antigen recognized by monocloal antibody AE3, is a sulfoglycoprotein and a sulfoglycosylceramide, both of which contain the monosulfate of a disialylated tetrasaccharide.
antibody AE3 recognizes an epitope on the monosulphated tetra-gycosyl ceramide (SM1a, Gal beta 1-3 GalNAc beta 1-4(2-O-sulfate)-Gal beta 1- 4 GlcCer).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antigen recognized in AE3 immunohistochemistry is a carbohydrate sequence, and that the most likely source is a sulfoglycoconjugate.
the carbohydrate antigenic determinants of HCA are not unique, but are shared by a number of glycolipid and glycoprotein structures.

we have established that the antigenic determinant for the monoclonal antibody, AE3, is a monosulfated disaccharide, βGalNAc(3S)Gal, which is present as a terminal structure on a sulfoganglioside and also as a part of mucin glycoproteins in human epithelial cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carbohydrate microarray technology is a powerful tool to identify the antigenic determinant of a monoclonal antibody.
the HCA antigen recognized by antibody 3 is a carbohydrate, and not a protein, and that it is a sulfoglycan, not a glycoprotein.

the carbohydrate sequence recognized by AE3 is not the same as the carbohydrate sequence recognized in the sera of patients by the monoclonal antibody B72.3, and that the antigen is not the carbohydrate epitope that is recognized by the monoclonals MA-1 and MA-3.
